This breaks the single-model RL saturation ceiling and offers a new post-training paradigm for dense-reward domains like code and reasoning. The adaptive multi-teacher on-policy distillation method also provides a parameter-efficient way to integrate multi-expert strengths.
summary_en.technical_approach: CHORUS is a three-stage post-training framework for testbench stimulus generation: 1) It retains all intermediate checkpoints from staged SFT, and applies the same execution-guided RL procedure to each independently (optimized with DAPO, jointly training direct generation and agentic refinement modes, with rewards derived from simulator coverage signals), producing multiple experts with similar aggregate performance but complementary task-level advantages. 2) Two expert consolidation schemes are provided: training-free weight averaging delivers immediate gains, while adaptive multi-teacher on-policy distillation selects the highest-reward expert per task as teacher, and only distills when the teacher outperforms the student to avoid degrading behavior.
summary_en.experiments: The final 4B-parameter model achieves 88.0% Pass@1 on the CVDP-ECov benchmark, 13.5 percentage points higher than the 671B-parameter DeepSeek-R1. Experiments confirm that RL-trained experts from staged SFT checkpoints are indeed complementary (different experts excel on different tasks, with large coverage gaps on disagreed tasks), and both consolidation schemes surpass the single-expert saturation point.
summary_en.reading_guide: For a quick read, start with the core observations in the introduction (single-model RL saturation, value of staged SFT diversity) and Figure 2 for the framework overview. Then read Section 3 for the method, focusing on complementary expert generation and adaptive multi-teacher distillation. For experiments, look at the main results and analysis of expert complementarity. Estimated reading time: ~20 minutes.

recommendation.zh: 核心 insight 是 staged SFT 产生互补专家再合并，对 RL 后训练中如何利用行为多样性有参考价值，重点看专家多样性与合并策略那一节。
recommendation.en: The key insight is using staged SFT to produce complementary experts then merging them; useful for leveraging behavioral diversity in RL post-training—focus on the expert diversity and merging section.

paper.title: Critic-Free Pretraining for Efficient Online Reinforcement Learning Fine-Tuning
paper.abstract: Offline-to-online (O2O) reinforcement learning aims to leverage policies pretrained on static datasets while improving them through online interaction. However, directly reusing an offline-trained critic can hinder online fine-tuning: as the policy and data distribution change rapidly, value estimates inherited from offline training may become misaligned with the online environment, leading to inaccurate policy improvement and inefficient exploration. To address this problem, we introduce \textb

summary.core_problem: 离线到在线强化学习中，直接复用离线训练 critic 可能在在线分布快速变化时产生错误价值估计，拖慢 fine-tuning 和探索。
summary.importance: 贡献类型是 RL 训练范式修正。它提出不要预训练 critic，而让在线阶段的新 critic 从零适应环境；对 LLM RLHF/RLVR 的间接启发是，继承一个分布外 value/reward 估计器未必比重新学习更稳。
summary.technical_approach: 提出 Critic-Free Pretraining。离线阶段不训练或不继承 critic，只保留可迁移的 policy 预训练；在线阶段使用 freshly initialized critic，让价值函数跟随新数据分布重新估计。方法宣称可插入多种主流 offline-to-online RL 算法。
summary.experiments: 摘要称在多类任务上，CFP 与常规 O2O 算法持平或更好，在若干困难任务上提升更明显。摘要未说明任务集合、policy/critic 网络规模、离线数据质量、baseline 名称或具体提升幅度。

summary_en.core_problem: In offline-to-online reinforcement learning, reusing an offline-trained critic can produce misaligned value estimates when the online policy and data distribution shift rapidly.
summary_en.importance: The contribution is a training-paradigm adjustment for RL. It argues that the critic should not be pretrained or inherited; instead, a fresh critic should adapt online. For LLM RLHF or RLVR, the indirect lesson is that carrying over an out-of-distribution value or reward estimator may hurt stability.
summary_en.technical_approach: The paper introduces Critic-Free Pretraining. The offline phase avoids training or reusing the critic and focuses on policy pretraining; the online phase initializes a new critic from scratch so value estimation tracks the new data distribution. The method is presented as compatible with several mainstream offline-to-online RL algorithms.
summary_en.experiments: The abstract claims that CFP matches or improves conventional O2O algorithms across diverse tasks, with stronger gains on several challenging tasks. It does not specify the task suite, model sizes, offline data regimes, baseline names, or numerical improvements.

recommendation.zh: 只看动机和消融即可；它给 RL 后训练一个有用警告：离线 critic 继承可能是负资产，但离 LLM setup 还远。
recommendation.en: Read only the motivation and ablations; it is a useful warning that inherited offline critics can be liabilities, but the setup is still far from LLM RL.

paper.title: Sci-VBench: Evaluating Knowledge- and Reasoning-Intensive Video Generation in Science Domains
paper.abstract: We introduce Sci-VBench, a comprehensive benchmark for evaluating knowledge- and reasoning-intensive video generation across scientific domains. It contains 1,253 expert-annotated examples spanning 60 subjects across four core disciplines: Natural Science, Healthcare, Humanities & Social Sciences, and Engineering. Each example requires models to generate temporally rich videos that demand scientific reasoning and knowledge-grounded synthesis, going beyond surface-level visual plausibility. We fu

summary.core_problem: 能否用因果语言模型（Causal LM）通过受限的 Token 生成，直接替代传统的特定任务回归、排序或策略 Head，来进行金融数值预测和资产配置？
summary.importance: 探索了将连续的金融数值预测和决策任务转化为离散的 Token 生成任务（Language Modeling 范式），为跨领域任务统一到自回归生成框架提供了实证支持。
summary.technical_approach: 提出 FinATOM，一个无 Head 的统一接口。预测模型自回归地生成经过波动率标准化的收益率 Token，并使用序数和排序监督进行训练，随后进行单 epoch 的 Token 级策略微调。配置模型生成归一化的只做多头权重；SFT 阶段模仿因果均值-方差锚点，随后使用 DAPO 增强的 GRPO 算法优化实际的 21 天夏普比率，并保持与锚点的一致性。
summary.experiments: 在 2023-2025 年的 ETF 测试中，配置策略将汇总的总夏普比率从 1.428 提升至 1.529，在 5bp 交易成本模型下的净夏普比率从 1.394 提升至 1.494。

summary_en.core_problem: Can a causal language model directly replace traditional task-specific regression, ranking, or policy heads for financial numerical prediction and asset allocation through constrained token generation?
summary_en.importance: Explores converting continuous financial numerical prediction and decision-making tasks into discrete token generation tasks (Language Modeling paradigm), providing empirical support for unifying cross-domain tasks into an autoregressive generation framework.
summary_en.technical_approach: Proposes FinATOM, a unified head-free interface. The forecasting model autoregressively emits volatility-standardized return tokens, trained with ordinal and ranking supervision, followed by a one-epoch token-level policy stage. The allocation model generates normalized long-only weights; SFT imitates a causal mean-variance anchor, and DAPO-augmented GRPO optimizes the realized 21-day Sharpe ratio subject to anchor consistency.
summary_en.experiments: In 2023-2025 ETF tests, the allocation policy improved the pooled gross Sharpe ratio from 1.428 to 1.529, and the net Sharpe ratio under a 5-bp transaction-cost model from 1.394 to 1.494.

recommendation.zh: 将连续数值预测和 RL 决策完全转化为离散 Token 的自回归生成，验证了 LM 范式在非自然语言/非视觉连续控制任务上的通用性，值得关注其 Token 化和 GRPO 优化的细节。
recommendation.en: Converts continuous numerical prediction and RL decision-making entirely into discrete token autoregressive generation, validating the universality of the LM paradigm on non-NLP/vision continuous control tasks. The details of tokenization and GRPO optimization are worth noting.

paper.title: DistillCache: KL-Guided Adaptive KV-Cache Eviction for Memory-Efficient LLM Inference
paper.abstract: Transformer-based large language models (LLMs) achieve strong performance across many tasks, but their Key-Value (KV) cache grows linearly with sequence length, creating a severe memory bottleneck for long-context inference. Existing heuristic eviction methods (e.g., H$_2$O and SnapKV) rely on static attention or positional signals that often fail to capture a token's future predictive influence. We propose DistillCache, a reinforcement learning framework that formulates KV-cache eviction as a s

summary.core_problem: 长上下文推理时 KV cache 随序列长度线性增长，现有静态驱逐规则难以判断哪些历史 token 会影响未来输出分布。
summary.importance: 这是推理内存优化方法贡献。它把 KV-cache 驱逐从手工启发式改写为序列决策问题，并用 full-cache 与 compressed-cache 输出分布的 KL 差异作为训练信号；对长上下文 serving 和训练时长上下文设计都有间接参考价值。
summary.technical_approach: 提出 DistillCache：训练一个轻量策略网络，根据 attention statistics、value norm、entropy、position 等内部信号决定逐步驱逐哪些 KV 条目。训练使用 REINFORCE，reward 来自每步 KL divergence，目标是让压缩缓存下的输出分布贴近 full-cache 模型。
summary.experiments: 实验在 Mistral-7B-Instruct-v0.3 上进行，评测 LongBench。摘要报告在 25% cache budget 下保留 full-cache accuracy 的 94.2%，优于 H2O、SnapKV 等静态或启发式驱逐基线；但只看到 7B 指令模型结果，未确认多模型、多上下文长度和策略训练开销的完整覆盖。

summary_en.core_problem: The paper tackles the linear growth of the KV cache in long-context LLM inference and the difficulty of deciding which cached tokens will matter for future predictions.
summary_en.importance: It is an inference-efficiency contribution. The main shift is to treat cache eviction as a learned sequential decision problem, with KL divergence to the full-cache output distribution as the preservation objective.
summary_en.technical_approach: DistillCache trains a lightweight policy network using internal model signals such as attention statistics, value norms, entropy, and position. The policy is optimized with REINFORCE, using a per-step KL reward to keep compressed-cache outputs close to full-cache outputs.
summary_en.experiments: The reported experiments use Mistral-7B-Instruct-v0.3 and LongBench. At a 25% cache budget, DistillCache retains 94.2% of full-cache accuracy and outperforms H2O and SnapKV according to the abstract. The provided information does not establish robustness across model families, longer contexts, or policy-training overhead.

recommendation.zh: 只看方法和 LongBench 表即可；KL 蒸馏信号合理，但单 7B setup 不足以改 KV 驱逐 prior。
recommendation.en: Read the method and LongBench table; the KL signal is sensible, but a single 7B setup is not enough to reset priors on KV eviction.

paper.title: DiDPO: Diff-in-Diff Policy Optimization for Coding Agent Training
paper.abstract: Reinforcement learning with Verifiable Reward (RLVR) has emerged as a powerful paradigm for training coding agents, where the execution feedback from compilation and tests provides objective verification. However, unlike agent tasks, coding agents face a unique and finer-grained credit assignment challenge: at each step, coding actions simultaneously pack varying changes into different regions of a code version, which makes the contribution of independent change indistinguishable. Existing RLVR

summary.core_problem: 在 coding agent 的 RLVR 训练中，单步动作往往对应一个包含多处修改的 code diff，导致 credit assignment 过粗：成功/失败的回报无法区分 diff 内不同子修改的贡献。论文要解决的是：不引入 critic、也不增加额外环境 rollouts 的情况下，如何把轨迹级回报细化到 diff 内部的子区域，并把更细粒度的优势信号回传到对应的响应 token。
summary.importance:
更偏 post-train / agent RL 的方法论文，对“预训练”本身影响间接，但对 pretrain↔posttrain 闭环有两点启发：
1）当动作天然是“打包的结构化编辑”（diff）时，直接用 outcome reward 或 step reward 会浪费可验证信号；需要把结构拆开再做优势分配。
2）它提供了一种不依赖 value critic 的细粒度 credit 构造方式，和 GRPO/DAPO/GSPO 这类 group-based policy optimization 的工程路线兼容，适合在大规模 RLVR 训练里控制不稳定性与成本。

是否值得投入取决于你的工作是否覆盖 coding agent 的 RL 训练；若主要做基座预训练/数据/优化，这篇更多是“了解一种 credit 细化的做法”，不太会直接改你的 pretrain recipe。
summary.technical_approach:
DiDPO 的核心是把“轨迹级 group-relative advantage”继续向下分解到 diff 内部。

设定上沿用 CodeAct 式 Thought-Action-Observation 循环：每步 action 产生一次代码编辑（add/del/none），环境给 outcome reward（例如测试是否通过）。传统做法把整段响应当作一个 credit 载体；GiGPO 会按相似 state/action 分组做 state-level advantage，但 coding 的关键困难是：同一步 diff 里可能包含多个功能区域的修改。

DiDPO 做了三件事：
1）跨 rollouts 对齐 diff：对同一任务 prompt 采样多条轨迹，比较相邻版本之间的 diffs，在不同 rollout 的 diffs 中寻找“高度相似的 sub-diff”作为 anchor。
2）用 anchor 诱导 sub-diff 边界：把一个大 diff 切成若干 sub-diff，使这些 sub-diff 更像可复用的功能单元（例如某个函数、某段逻辑、某处 import/配置）。
3）sub-diff 分组并计算 diff-level advantage：把对齐后的 sub-diff 组成局部 group，计算局部的 group-relative advantage（diff-level advantage），再与轨迹级 advantage 结合，并投影回生成这些 sub-diff 的 token 上更新策略。

为避免 anchor 过大（语义太杂）或过小（难以聚合成组），论文引入 groupability score 来选择 anchor，平衡语义覆盖与可形成足够样本量的分组。

整体上它是 critic-free 的：优势来自组内相对比较，而不是学习一个 value function；并且强调“不需要额外 rollouts”，即在同一批采样轨迹上做更细的对齐与分配。
summary.experiments:
论文声称在多个 long-horizon coding benchmark 上优于现有 coding/agentic RL baselines（文中提到的对比对象包括 GRPO、DAPO、GSPO、GiGPO 等路线，以及一些 coding agent 相关方法）。但当前提供的正文片段未包含：具体 benchmark 名称与规模、基座模型大小、训练步数/rollout 数、pass@k 或 repo-repair 成功率的绝对值与提升幅度、以及关键消融（没有 sub-diff advantage / 没有 groupability / 不同对齐策略）的数字。

精读时建议重点核对两类结果：
- 细粒度 credit 是否真的带来稳定收益，还是主要来自某种隐含的“更强的样本筛选/重加权”；
- 计算开销：diff 对齐与相似度计算在大规模 RLVR 下是否成为瓶颈。
summary.reading_guide:
泛读建议：
1）先读 Introduction 里对 coding 与一般 agent action 的三点差异（diff 打包、sub-diff 功能混杂、语法/执行约束），这是方法动机的关键。
2）再读 Problem Setting，确认它沿用的 group-relative advantage 形式，以及与 GiGPO 的关系。
3）方法部分重点看：sub-diff anchor 如何定义“相似”、边界如何诱导、groupability score 的具体形式，以及 token-level credit 如何回传。
4）实验部分优先找消融：没有对齐/没有 groupability/只用 trajectory advantage 的对比。

预计阅读时间：20–30 分钟可把方法主线读懂；若要落地实现，需要额外时间看 diff 相似度与对齐的工程细节。

summary_en.core_problem: In RLVR training for coding agents, a single step often produces a bundled code diff touching multiple regions, making credit assignment too coarse. The paper targets fine-grained credit assignment inside a diff—down to aligned sub-diffs—without using a critic and without requiring extra environment rollouts.
summary_en.importance:
This is a post-training / agent-RL contribution rather than pretraining. The relevance to foundation-model training is indirect but practical if you run large-scale RLVR: (1) it argues that outcome/step rewards waste verifiable signal when actions are structured edits; (2) it offers a critic-free way to construct finer advantages compatible with group-based policy optimization (GRPO/DAPO/GSPO-style), potentially improving stability/cost.

If your focus is core pretraining (data/optimizer/scaling), this is more of a technique to be aware of than something that changes pretrain recipes.
summary_en.technical_approach:
DiDPO extends group-relative advantage from the trajectory level into the internal structure of a code diff.

Using a CodeAct-like interaction loop, each action yields an edit (add/del/none) and the environment provides an outcome reward (e.g., tests pass/fail). Instead of treating the whole response/diff as one credit carrier, DiDPO:
1) Aligns diffs across multiple rollouts for the same task by finding highly similar sub-diffs that recur across trajectories.
2) Uses these recurring sub-diffs as anchors to induce sub-diff boundaries within larger diffs, aiming to isolate functional regions.
3) Groups aligned sub-diffs and computes a local group-relative advantage (diff-level advantage), then combines it with the trajectory-level advantage and assigns it back to the tokens responsible for generating those sub-diffs.

To avoid anchors that are too broad (mixing functions) or too narrow (hard to aggregate), it introduces a groupability score to select anchors that balance semantic scope and group mass. The method remains critic-free and claims no additional rollouts beyond the sampled group.
summary_en.experiments:
The paper reports consistent improvements over strong RLVR baselines (e.g., GRPO/DAPO/GSPO/GiGPO-style methods) on long-horizon coding benchmarks. However, the provided excerpt does not include the concrete experimental tables: benchmark list, model sizes, training budgets, absolute success rates/pass@k, and key ablations (removing sub-diff alignment, removing groupability scoring, using only trajectory-level advantage).

When reading the full experiments, the main checks are: whether gains persist across tasks and seeds, and whether diff alignment/similarity computation becomes a scalability bottleneck.
summary_en.reading_guide:
Skim plan:
- Read the introduction’s three properties distinguishing coding from generic agent RL; that is the real motivation.
- In the problem setting, confirm the baseline advantage formulation and how it relates to GiGPO.
- In the method section, focus on: how sub-diff similarity/anchors are defined, how boundaries are induced, what the groupability score is, and how token-level credit is assigned.
- In experiments, prioritize ablations isolating each component.

Time: ~20–30 minutes for the main idea; longer if you need implementation details for diff alignment.

recommendation.zh: 将 RL 的 reward 粒度下钻到 code diff 级别是个很直觉且 necessary 的改进，值得关注其具体的 diff 构造和 credit assignment 算法设计。
recommendation.en: Drilling down the RL reward granularity to the code diff level is an intuitive and necessary improvement; the specific diff construction and credit assignment algorithm design are worth examining.

paper.title: Trajectory-Relative Hindsight Distillation for Agentic Reinforcement Learning
paper.abstract: Recent agentic reinforcement learning methods use hindsight to complement sparse outcome rewards. However, a completed rollout can yield many such signals, leaving their appropriate allocation across turns unclear. We introduce TRIAL, a trajectory-relative hindsight distillation framework with a unified turn-aligned scoring protocol. For each decision turn, TRIAL extracts an outcome view of that decision's realized consequence and evaluates the same response under ordinary and hindsight-conditio

summary.core_problem: TRIAL 解决的是 agentic RL 中稀疏结果奖励和多轮决策之间的信用分配问题。一次完整 rollout 只有最终成功或失败信号，但轨迹里包含多个决策 turn。已有 hindsight distillation 能给每个已执行动作构造事后监督，却没有清楚回答一个问题：这些 dense hindsight 信号应该在不同 turn 之间如何分配强度。
summary.importance: 这项工作和预训练训练流程的关系较间接，但对 RL 后训练、长程 agent 训练和 verifier/reward 信号设计有启发。它把 hindsight 信号拆成两个层次：token 级别的方向由 log-prob gap 决定，turn 级别的权重由整条轨迹内的相对 revision magnitude 决定。这个设计比简单给所有 hindsight token 同权更稳，因为它控制了平均权重，同时允许关键 turn 获得更大训练强度。对需要把长程交互数据转成可训练监督信号的系统，这是一种可复用的 credit allocation recipe。
summary.technical_approach: TRIAL 保留 GRPO 的 rollout-level outcome advantage 和 clipping 规则，在此基础上加入一个训练时 hindsight objective。对每个决策 turn，方法构造一个 outcome view，把该决策实际导致的局部后果暴露给 scorer。然后用同一个已生成 response，在 ordinary context 和 hindsight-conditioned context 下分别计算 token log probability。两者的有符号差值决定 token 更新方向和局部强度。接着，TRIAL 汇总每个 turn 内 eligible tokens 的绝对 gap，并和该 turn 在整条轨迹中的 eligible-token 占比比较，得到 trajectory-relative allocation multiplier。这些 multiplier 的 eligible-token 加权平均值被归一为 1，因此它是在固定平均训练强度下重新分配 hindsight 监督。最后，dense hindsight loss 与 GRPO loss 结合，并用相对 detached GRPO loss magnitude 的 scalar clamp 控制 dense 项强度。所有 hindsight context 和分配 profile 只在训练时使用，部署时不增加推理开销。
summary.experiments: 实验在 WebShop 和 ALFWorld 上进行，backbone 包括 Qwen2.5-3B 和 Qwen3-1.7B。TRIAL 在 backbone、环境和指标组成的 8 个组合中都优于 GRPO；和 5 个 baseline 比较时，在 6 个 case 中最好或并列最好。WebShop 上使用 Qwen3-1.7B 时，success rate 从 GRPO 的 56.4% 提升到 75.2%，task score 从 78.7% 提升到 85.7%。消融实验固定 hindsight pathway，只替换 turn allocation profile。trajectory-relative profile 在 WebShop 和 ALFWorld 的 4 个指标上都优于 unit profile，说明收益不只是来自 dense hindsight distillation，还来自轨迹内相对权重分配。source-shuffled profile 的对照也支持 profile 和真实轨迹结构相关，而不是简单噪声正则化。
summary.reading_guide: 建议泛读 25–35 分钟。先看 Method 中对 signed token gap、eligible-token mask、turn-level magnitude 和 trajectory-normalized multiplier 的定义；这是全文核心。再看 Figure 2，理解 GRPO outcome supervision 和 TRIAL hindsight supervision 如何并行工作。实验部分重点看 WebShop/Qwen3-1.7B 的提升，以及 unit profile、source-shuffled profile 的消融。若关注 RL 训练稳定性，可以额外看 dense loss clamp 的处理方式，它反映了作者在不破坏 GRPO advantage construction 的前提下加入辅助信号的取舍。

summary_en.core_problem: TRIAL addresses credit allocation in agentic reinforcement learning. A multi-turn rollout usually receives a sparse final outcome reward, but the trajectory contains many decisions made under different observations. Hindsight distillation can provide dense supervision for realized actions, yet it leaves open how much of that supervision should be assigned to each turn.
summary_en.importance: The work is most relevant to RL post-training and long-horizon agent training rather than pretraining itself. Its useful idea is to separate token-level revision direction from turn-level allocation. The signed log-probability gap gives local token supervision, while a trajectory-relative profile decides which turns deserve more weight. This is a practical recipe for converting long interaction traces into calibrated training signals without simply giving every hindsight token the same weight.
summary_en.technical_approach: TRIAL keeps the GRPO rollout-level advantage and clipping rule unchanged, then adds a training-only hindsight objective. For each decision turn, it builds an outcome view that exposes the realized local consequence of that decision. The same generated response is scored under the ordinary interaction context and under the hindsight-conditioned context. The signed token-level log-probability gap determines update direction and local revision strength. TRIAL then aggregates absolute gaps within each turn and compares a turn’s share of total revision magnitude with its share of eligible tokens. This yields a trajectory-relative allocation multiplier. The multipliers are normalized so their eligible-token-weighted mean is one, which redistributes hindsight supervision while keeping the average allocation fixed. A scalar clamp bounds the dense loss contribution relative to the detached GRPO loss magnitude. Hindsight contexts, discrepancy scores, and allocation profiles are used only during training, so inference uses the ordinary policy.
summary_en.experiments: The experiments use WebShop and ALFWorld with Qwen2.5-3B and Qwen3-1.7B. TRIAL improves over GRPO in all eight combinations of model, environment, and metric, and is best or tied best among six methods in six cases. On WebShop with Qwen3-1.7B, success rate increases from 56.4% to 75.2%, and task score increases from 78.7% to 85.7%. Controlled ablations keep the hindsight pathway fixed and vary only the allocation profile. The trajectory-relative profile outperforms a unit profile on all four WebShop and ALFWorld metrics, showing that the gains are not just from dense hindsight supervision. The source-shuffled profile comparison further suggests that the allocation profile benefits from being aligned with the actual trajectory structure.
summary_en.reading_guide: A 25–35 minute skim is appropriate. Focus on the method definitions for signed token gaps, eligible-token masks, turn-level magnitudes, and trajectory-normalized multipliers. Figure 2 is the quickest way to understand how TRIAL complements GRPO rather than replacing it. In the experiments, prioritize the WebShop result with Qwen3-1.7B and the ablations comparing trajectory-relative, unit, and source-shuffled profiles. For readers interested in RL training stability, the loss clamp is worth checking because it shows how the auxiliary dense signal is constrained without changing GRPO’s advantage construction.

recommendation.zh: hindsight奖励分配的实用改进，对做agent RL或推理RL的研究员有参考，重点看§3的评分协议设计。
recommendation.en: Practical improvement for hindsight reward allocation, useful for researchers working on agent RL or reasoning RL, focus on the scoring protocol in §3.

paper.title: Fisher-R1: Training LLM Agents for Reliable Hypothesis Testing
paper.abstract: Reliable hypothesis testing is the foundation of many empirical scientific claims. Large language model (LLM) agents are increasingly used to automate this process, as they can inspect datasets, generate code, and produce analyses end-to-end. However, we show that they frequently make subtle inferential errors that lead to incorrect conclusions despite correctly executed analyses. Existing benchmarks fail to capture this failure mode, as they rarely assess whether a reported p-value is statistic

summary.core_problem: LLM coding agent 在做开放式假设检验时，经常能写出可运行代码并得到数值结果，但会在统计方法选择、前提假设检查和结论推断上出错，导致 p 值和结论在统计上无效；现有数据分析 benchmark 没有系统评估这种“代码能跑但推断错误”的失效模式。
summary.importance: 对预训练主线的直接启发有限，更接近特定科研 agent 能力评测与 post-training。但论文指出的问题有方法论意义：很多 agent benchmark 只验证“有没有执行出结果”，而不验证“执行的方法是否对应该问题和数据生成假设”。这一点和预训练后“模型能生成流畅回答但推理链/验证链不可靠”是同类评估缺口。对做 agent/RM/verifier、尤其是 code-and-tool-use agent 的研究者有参考价值；对纯基座预训练读者，可作为“评测必须验证过程合法性而非只看终态答案”的案例。
summary.technical_approach: 构建 P-Bench，包含 425 个开放式假设检验任务，覆盖经济学、生物学、医学等真实科学数据。每个任务提供问题、数据集和数据描述，agent 需要在 R 执行环境中多轮交互，自行选择统计方法、运行分析、报告 p 值并给出拒绝/不拒绝原假设的结论。答案以可执行的参考分析为基础，经过领域专家审核，重点比对方法选择、p 值准确性和结论正确性，而非只看代码是否运行或报告是否流畅。在此基础上训练 Fisher-R1：先用合成生成的、带验证答案的假设检验任务做 SFT，再用基于结果正确性的 RL 训练。
summary.experiments: P-Bench 共 425 个任务，来源于同行评议论文和权威生物统计教学材料，答案键绑定到可执行参考分析。Fisher-R1-14B 在该 benchmark 上报告超过 GPT-5.4 与 DeepSeek-V4-Pro；论文展示的典型失效是模型识别到异常值/模型误设等警告信号，但仍选择错误的检验方法（如在高杠杆点存在时继续用线性回归而改用秩检验），从而得到显著但不可靠的 p 值。实验重点在 p 值准确性和结论正确性两个维度，而不是一般数据问答任务上的通过率。
summary.reading_guide: 泛读。重点看引言里的失效模式例子（识别警告但做错误方法选择）、P-Bench 的任务设计与答案构造方式，以及为什么要把“方法选择 + p 值 + 结论”绑定在可执行参考分析上，而不是只让评委看自然语言报告。训练部分对纯预训练读者不是重点；若关心 agent post-training，可看合成任务生成和 outcome-grounded RL 的设计。预计阅读时间 15–20 分钟。

summary_en.core_problem: LLM coding agents can often produce runnable code and numerical outputs for open-ended hypothesis-testing tasks, yet still make subtle inferential mistakes—choosing the wrong test, ignoring modeling assumptions, or drawing invalid conclusions—so the reported p-values are not statistically valid; existing data-analysis benchmarks do not systematically measure this failure mode.
summary_en.importance: The paper is not a core pretraining contribution and sits closer to domain-specific agent evaluation and post-training. Its broader relevance is methodological: many agent benchmarks reward executable workflows or plausible final answers without checking whether the chosen procedure is actually valid given the question and data-generating assumptions. This is the same class of evaluation gap that appears whenever fluent generation masks flawed reasoning or unverified tool use. It is useful for researchers working on agents, verifiers, reward modeling, and code-and-tool use; for pure pretraining readers it mainly serves as a concrete example that evaluation must validate procedural correctness, not just end-state answers.
summary_en.technical_approach: The paper introduces P-Bench, a benchmark of 425 open-ended hypothesis-testing tasks built from real scientific datasets across economics, biology, and medicine. For each task the agent receives a scientific question, a dataset, and a description, and must interact with an R execution environment across multiple turns to choose a statistical method, run the analysis, report a p-value, and decide whether to reject the null. Answer keys are grounded in logged executions of canonical reference analyses and audited by domain experts, scoring method choice, p-value accuracy, and conclusion correctness rather than code executability or report fluency alone. Fisher-R1 is then trained by supervised fine-tuning on synthetically generated hypothesis-testing tasks with verified keys, followed by reinforcement learning using outcome-grounded rewards.
summary_en.experiments: P-Bench contains 425 tasks drawn from peer-reviewed papers and authoritative biostatistics teaching materials, with answer keys tied to executable reference analyses. Fisher-R1-14B is reported to outperform strong baselines including GPT-5.4 and DeepSeek-V4-Pro on P-Bench. A representative failure case is that frontier agents can recognize warning signs such as high-leverage outliers but still proceed with an inappropriate test—for example, using linear regression where a rank-based test is required—producing a runnable analysis and fluent narrative with an invalid, yet statistically significant-looking, p-value. The main evaluation axes are p-value accuracy and conclusion correctness rather than generic data-analysis task completion.
summary_en.reading_guide: Skim this paper. Focus on the introduction for the motivating failure mode—recognizing diagnostic warnings while making the wrong inferential choice—and on the P-Bench design, especially why answer keys must be tied to executable reference analyses that score method, p-value, and conclusion jointly instead of grading natural-language reports in isolation. The training recipe for Fisher-R1 is secondary unless you work on agent post-training; if so, look at the synthetic task generator and outcome-grounded RL setup. Estimated reading time: 15–20 minutes.

recommendation.zh: P-Bench 对做 agent 评测的人有参考价值，Fisher-R1 的 RL 训练 recipe 可看，但核心是统计推断这个特定垂直场景，通用 pretrain 启发有限。
recommendation.en: P-Bench is useful for agent evaluation researchers and Fisher-R1's RL recipe is worth a look, but the statistical-inference vertical limits general pretraining insight.

paper.title: RRC: Unlocking Generative Reward Models in LLM Reinforcement Learning via Ranking-Based Reward Construction
paper.abstract: Recent advances in reward modeling show a paradigm shift from discriminative reward models to generative reward models. However, despite their strong capabilities in response ranking, generative reward models have not realized their potential in reinforcement learning (RL). Our analysis reveals that this limitation arises from a mismatch between the comparative nature of generative reward modeling and the scalar scoring paradigm adopted by existing RL algorithms. To bridge this gap, we propose a

summary.core_problem: 论文解决的是生成式 reward model 在 LLM 强化学习中用不好的问题。生成式 reward model 擅长比较两个或多个回答并给出文字化判断，但现有 RL 算法通常需要每个回答一个标量 reward。把生成式模型强行转成 token probability 或无推理的偏好 token，会丢掉它在比较、解释和 test-time compute 上的优势。
summary.importance: 这篇与 post-train/RL 训练信号质量直接相关，适合泛读。它的主要启发是：reward 不一定要由 reward model 直接输出标量，也可以先让模型做它更擅长的排序，再把排序结构转换成 RL 可用的标量。这个思路对 RLHF/RLAIF、reasoning RL 和 generative verifier 都有参考意义。尤其是推理型任务中，生成式 judge 的 CoT 和多次推理可能提高偏好判断质量，但需要一个与策略优化兼容的接口。RRC 给出了一个较清晰的接口设计。
summary.technical_approach: 方法叫 Ranking-based Reward Construction，核心是只让生成式 reward model 做相对排序，不要求它直接给单样本标量分数。论文提出两种机制。第一是 self-competitive ranking：对同一个 prompt 下当前 policy 采样出的多个回答进行相互比较，得到相对质量顺序，再把排名映射为 reward。这样 reward 来自同批样本内部的竞争关系，适合 GRPO 这类组内相对优化方法。第二是 anchor-guided ranking：引入少量 anchor responses 作为参考点，让每个候选回答与 anchor 比较，降低大规模样本排序时的调用成本。论文给出的复杂度从约 O(m log m) 的排序式比较转为 O(m n)，其中 m 是候选回答数，n 是 anchor 数；当 n 很小时，扩展性更好。构造出的 reward 可以接入 GRPO 和 DAPO 等现有 RL 算法。与 GenRM 使用指定 preference token 概率不同，RRC 不依赖单个 token 概率；与 GRAM 去掉显式 CoT 不同，RRC 允许生成式 reward model 保留文字判断和推理过程。
summary.experiments: 实验覆盖 6 个 benchmark，包括 open-ended chat 和 reasoning 任务。相对 probability-based reward baseline，RRC 带来稳定提升：AlpacaEval2 从 35.8% 提升到 41.3%，ArenaHardV2 从 8.0% 提升到 11.2%，MMLU-Redux 从 52.9% 提升到 57.3%。论文还报告了两个 scaling 方向：增加生成式 reward model 的 inference-time computation 可以提升 RL 表现；增加 anchor responses 数量也能改善 reward 构造质量。附录 A 给出理论分析，说明基于排序的 reward 构造能放宽直接标量 reward 的约束，从而提高可达到的优化上限。需要注意的是，方法会增加 reward 侧推理调用，实际训练成本取决于候选数、anchor 数和 judge 推理长度。
summary.reading_guide: 建议泛读，约 35–45 分钟。先看 Introduction 中对 discriminative reward、GenRM/GRAM 和 generative reward mismatch 的分析。方法部分重点看 self-competitive ranking 与 anchor-guided ranking 如何把相对排序映射成标量 reward，以及它们如何接入 GRPO/DAPO。实验部分重点看六个 benchmark 的主结果表、inference-time compute scaling 曲线和 anchor 数量消融。附录 A 可选择性阅读，主要用于理解作者为什么认为排序 reward 的可优化空间大于直接标量 reward。若关注训练成本，应重点检查 reward model 调用次数、CoT 长度和不同 sample size 下的效率曲线。

summary_en.core_problem: The paper addresses why generative reward models have not translated well into LLM reinforcement learning. These models are naturally good at comparative judgment: given multiple responses, they can decide which is better and explain why. Standard RL pipelines, however, expect one scalar reward per response. Converting a generative judge into a scalar through preference-token probability, or removing explicit reasoning to emit only a label, underuses the model’s comparative and test-time reasoning strengths.
summary_en.importance: This is a useful skim for post-training and RL signal design. The main idea is that a reward model does not have to emit scalar rewards directly. It can first perform the operation it is better suited for—ranking responses—and the ranking can then be converted into scalar rewards for policy optimization. This is relevant to RLHF, RLAIF, reasoning RL, and generative verifiers. It gives a practical interface between generative judges with chain-of-thought style evaluation and existing algorithms such as GRPO or DAPO.
summary_en.technical_approach: The proposed method is Ranking-based Reward Construction. It uses a generative reward model only for relative preference ranking, then derives scalar rewards from the resulting order. The first mechanism is self-competitive ranking: for a given prompt, multiple responses sampled from the current policy are compared against each other, and their relative order is mapped into rewards. This aligns naturally with group-relative policy optimization. The second mechanism is anchor-guided ranking: a small set of anchor responses serves as reference points, and candidate responses are compared against these anchors. This reduces the reward-model call pattern for larger candidate sets from a sorting-style O(m log m) regime to O(m n), where m is the number of sampled responses and n is the number of anchors. When n is small, this is more scalable. Unlike GenRM-style preference-token probabilities, RRC does not rely on a single token probability. Unlike approaches that suppress reasoning and emit only labels, it can preserve the generative judge’s textual reasoning process.
summary_en.experiments: The experiments cover 6 benchmarks spanning open-ended chat and reasoning tasks. Compared with probability-based reward baselines, RRC improves AlpacaEval2 from 35.8% to 41.3%, ArenaHardV2 from 8.0% to 11.2%, and MMLU-Redux from 52.9% to 57.3%. The paper also reports two useful scaling behaviors: RL performance improves when the generative reward model is given more inference-time computation, and it improves as the number of anchor responses increases. Appendix A provides a theoretical analysis suggesting that ranking-based reward construction relaxes constraints imposed by direct scalar rewards. The main practical caveat is reward-side cost: the method adds judge calls, and the actual training overhead depends on the number of candidates, the number of anchors, and the length of generated reasoning.
summary_en.reading_guide: Skim in about 35–45 minutes. Start with the Introduction’s diagnosis of the mismatch between generative reward modeling and scalar-reward RL. In the method section, focus on how self-competitive ranking and anchor-guided ranking convert relative order into scalar rewards, and how those rewards are plugged into GRPO or DAPO. In the experiments, prioritize the main benchmark table, the inference-time-compute scaling curves, and the anchor-count ablations. Appendix A is optional but useful for understanding the claimed optimization advantage of ranking-derived rewards. Readers concerned with training practicality should inspect the reward-model call counts, reasoning length, and sample-size efficiency details.

recommendation.zh: 做RLHF/RLVR的研究员重点看§3的范式不匹配分析和排序奖励设计，可直接复现用到内部GRM-RL pipeline
recommendation.en: For RLHF/RLVR researchers, focus on §3 paradigm mismatch analysis and ranking-based reward design; directly reproducible for internal GRM-RL pipelines

paper.title: LC-GRPO: Bridging Train-Inference Gap for Flow-Based GRPO with Langevin Correction
paper.abstract: Flow-based generative models are typically sampled by solving a deterministic ordinary differential equation (ODE), whereas online reinforcement learning requires stochastic rollouts for policy exploration and optimization. Existing GRPO methods for flow models therefore replace the inference-time ODE with a stochastic differential equation (SDE) during training. Although the ODE and SDE share the same marginal distributions in continuous time, their finite-step discretizations can differ substa

summary.core_problem: 流模型在推理时用确定性ODE采样，但在线RL训练需要随机rollout；用SDE替代会引入有限步离散化偏差，导致训练-推理分布不一致与样本变糊。
summary.importance: 属于“训练-推理 gap / on-policy RL 与生成采样器不一致”的通用问题；虽然对象是flow生成模型而非LLM，但对RL信号质量、采样器一致性这类post-train接口有可迁移的工程启示。
summary.technical_approach: 提出LC-GRPO：每步先做与推理一致的ODE Euler步，再做随机Langevin校正，使转移后的边缘分布对齐目标时刻；需要用score（梯度）来构造Langevin correction，从而在保持探索随机性的同时减少与ODE采样的偏差。
summary.experiments: 摘要未给出具体数据集/指标/提升幅度；只陈述SDE噪声增大导致rollout变糊、与测试ODE采样不匹配，并声称LC可缓解。

summary_en.core_problem: Flow models use deterministic ODE sampling at inference, but online RL needs stochastic rollouts; replacing ODE with SDE introduces finite-step discretization bias, causing a train–inference mismatch and blurry samples.
summary_en.importance: A general train–inference gap issue at the RL–sampler interface; while not an LLM paper, it offers transferable lessons on keeping RL training trajectories aligned with the deployment sampler.
summary_en.technical_approach: LC-GRPO: each rollout transition takes an inference-aligned ODE Euler step, then applies a stochastic Langevin correction targeting the marginal at that timestep; requires a score estimate to implement the correction, aiming to preserve exploration while reducing mismatch to the ODE sampler.
summary_en.experiments: The abstract provides no concrete datasets/metrics/gains; it motivates the method by noting SDE rollouts get blurrier with higher exploration noise and diverge from test-time ODE sampling.

recommendation.zh: 不是LLM，但“RL训练轨迹要对齐部署采样器”的点很实在；只看方法段落理解ODE步+Langevin校正的组合即可。
recommendation.en: Not LLM-focused, but the lesson “RL rollouts must match the deployed sampler” is practical; read only the method for the ODE-step + Langevin-correction construction.

paper.title: Search2Skill: Skill Distillation Beyond Knowledge Boundaries Via Rubric-Based Reinforcement Learning
paper.abstract: Reusable skills, which encapsulate the procedural knowledge required to solve real-world professional tasks, offer LLM-based agents a path toward self-evolution in expert domains. Existing self-evolving skill methods construct skills internally from the model's parametric knowledge or trajectories, and are therefore bounded by what the model already knows. However, the domain conventions and standard procedures underlying professional skills often lie beyond this boundary and are hard to elicit

summary.core_problem: 现有自进化 skill 方法依赖模型自身参数知识或轨迹，无法获取模型知识边界之外的专业领域规范与标准流程。
summary.importance: 方法创新：通过外部搜索填补能力缺口，并用 rubric-based RL 联合优化何时搜、怎么搜、怎么生成 skill。
summary.technical_approach: Search2Skill 自动识别 agent 能力缺口 → 外部搜索证据 → 蒸馏为结构化可复用 skill；用基于 rubric 的强化学习同时优化搜索时机、搜索策略与 skill 生成。
summary.experiments: 在 8 个专家级领域、3 个 benchmark 上验证，相比内部构造 skill 的方法在专业任务上表现更好。

summary_en.core_problem: Existing self-evolving skill methods rely on the model's parametric knowledge or trajectories and cannot acquire domain conventions and standard procedures beyond the model's knowledge boundary.
summary_en.importance: Method innovation: fills capability gaps via external search and uses rubric-based RL to jointly optimize when to search, how to search, and how to generate skills.
summary_en.technical_approach: Search2Skill automatically identifies agent capability gaps, searches external sources for evidence, and distills it into structured reusable skills; a rubric-based RL scheme jointly optimizes search timing, search strategy, and skill generation.
summary_en.experiments: Evaluated on eight expert-level domains across three benchmarks, outperforming methods that build skills internally from parametric knowledge.

recommendation.zh: agent 自进化 + 外部检索的常规组合，rubric-based RL 是亮点但非预训练核心，看方法节即可。
recommendation.en: A standard combination of agent self-evolution and external retrieval; rubric-based RL is the main novelty but not core to pretraining—read the method section only.

paper.title: SpecRoll: Fast-Slow Verifier-Feedback Adaptation for Speculative Reinforcement Learning Rollouts
paper.abstract: Reinforcement learning (RL) post-training improves the reasoning capabilities of large language models, but autoregressive rollout generation remains a major efficiency bottleneck. Speculative decoding can accelerate generation, yet applying it during RL is difficult because the target policy continually evolves: static proposers become stale, while frequent drafter updates add substantial overhead. We introduce SpecRoll, a speculative rollout engine that preserves the target model's sampling di

summary.core_problem: 这篇工作处理的是 RL post-training 里一个很具体但很关键的瓶颈：GRPO 这类 group-based RL 需要反复生成长 rollout，而 rollout 生成仍是逐 token 的主耗时。把 speculative decoding 直接搬到 RL 里并不顺，因为 target policy 在训练中持续漂移，静态 drafter 很快过时；如果像 FastGRPO 那样在线训练一个独立 drafter，又会引入额外反向传播、优化器状态、同步和 KV cache 成本。论文要解决的核心问题，是在不改变目标采样分布、不过多增加训练系统复杂度的前提下，让 speculative rollout 能适应 RL 中的非平稳策略，并在 wall-clock 上稳定提速。
summary.importance: 对预训练研究本身，它不是直接改 pretrain objective，但对 pretrain↔post-train 接口很有参考价值，尤其是大模型后训练阶段的系统效率问题。它的重要性主要有三点。第一，它把“精确 speculative decoding”从静态推理场景推进到在线变化的 RL rollout 场景，说明 rollout engine 也可以作为训练算法的一部分被设计。第二，它提出了两时间尺度适应：局部、无梯度、轨迹内修正处理短期失配；慢速参数更新处理持续漂移。这种分层适应思路，对持续预训练、mid-training、online data selection 也有启发。第三，它避免了单独训练一个 autoregressive drafter，而是用 target hidden state 上的 lightweight future-token heads 做 proposal，这在工程上更轻，也更接近“在主模型内部长出辅助预测头”的路线。
summary.technical_approach:
方法核心是一个 exact speculative rollout engine，名字叫 SpecRoll。它由四个部件组成。

第一，proposal family 不是独立 drafter，而是挂在 target backbone hidden state 上的多 horizon future-token heads，形式上接近 MEDUSA。给定前缀 x_{<=t}，target 先精确采样一个 anchor token x_{t+1}，然后多个 head 并行预测后续若干位置的 token，复用 target 的词表投影矩阵 W。这些候选组成一个 prefix-closed sparse tree。这样做的好处是省掉第二个 AR backbone 和对应 KV cache，proposal 成本更低，也减少了 target/drafter 失配来源。

第二，verification 是 exact 的，而且是 concurrency-aware 的。RL rollout 里同时活跃的样本数会随着部分样本提前结束而下降，因此固定大小的 speculative tree 在高并发阶段可能浪费验证算力，在低并发阶段又吃不满硬件。SpecRoll 会根据当前 active concurrency 动态调整 sparse tree 的预算：并发高时保守，减少额外验证负担；并发下降后扩大 tree，换取更高 accepted progress。论文的出发点不是单纯提高单条序列 acceptance，而是优化整个 GRPO rollout 阶段的吞吐。

第三，快路径是 Reflex。它利用“延迟 verifier 反馈在同一轨迹邻近位置上仍有预测性”这一观察，对 proposal hidden state 做 bounded、trajectory-local、gradient-free correction。这里的关键不是学习一个新模型，而是把已经成熟的 verifier error 当作局部校正信号，在不反传的情况下修正后续 proposal。为了避免误修正，作者加了 conservative alignment gate：只有当过去误差对未来仍有可预测性时才启用；同时还有 candidate-boundary safeguard，防止在候选边界附近做有害干预。这个设计试图区分 transient local mismatch 和 persistent drift：前者不值得动参数，局部修一下就够；后者才交给慢路径。

第四，慢路径只在 sustained degradation 被检测到时，才更新 future-token heads 的参数。也就是说，SpecRoll 不把所有失配都转成在线学习问题，而是先用 Reflex 吃掉短期、局部、轨迹内的偏差，把真正跨轨迹持续存在的 proposal 退化留给参数更新。这一点和 FastGRPO 的持续在线训练独立 drafter 不同，后者把适应主要放在参数层，代价更高，也不区分误差类型。

从训练目标上，SpecRoll 始终保持 exact target verification 为最终裁决，因此 committed token 的分布不变，GRPO 的 reward、advantage 和优化目标都不被改写。它优化的是 rollout 生成过程，而不是 RL objective 本身。
summary.experiments:
实验覆盖 5 个模型、参数规模从 1.5B 到 14B，3 个数学推理数据集，共 15 个 model-dataset 组合。主结果是：相对 vanilla GRPO，generation speedup 达到 1.26× 到 2.15×，end-to-end speedup 达到 1.21× 到 2.04×。和 FastGRPO 做 matched setting 对比时，SpecRoll 在全部 15 个组合上 generation 和 end-to-end 时间都更好，平均 pairwise end-to-end gain 为 1.18×。

这些数字说明两件事。第一，收益不只是 token generation microbenchmark 上的局部加速，而是能传导到完整 RL 训练回路。第二，轻量 proposal + 两时间尺度适应，至少在作者测试的规模和任务上，比“单独维护一个在线 drafter”更划算。

消融部分的关键信息是：快路径和慢路径都各自有贡献，组合时效果最好。也就是说，Reflex 并不是一个可有可无的小修补；它确实能吸收一部分短期失配。反过来，只有 Reflex 也不够，因为 policy drift 会跨轨迹累积，最终仍需要慢速参数更新。另一个值得注意的点是 concurrency-aware tree budget 的作用，它解释了为什么同样是 speculative decoding，在 RL rollout 里不能直接照搬固定树结构的推理配置。

从论文给出的结果看，作者更强调 wall-clock 和 end-to-end efficiency，而不是 reward 或 final accuracy 的显著变化。这是合理的，因为 exact verification 保证了采样分布不变，理论上训练信号应保持一致，主要差异体现在吞吐和系统开销上。
summary.reading_guide:
这篇适合泛读，但如果你做 RL 系统或 post-training infra，方法部分值得认真看。

建议先看 Introduction，抓住它和 FastGRPO 的分歧：不是再训练一个更聪明的 drafter，而是把适应拆成局部无梯度修正和低频参数更新。然后重点看 Figure 2 和 Method 里 proposal engine 的定义，理解 future-token heads、anchor token、sparse tree、exact verification 之间的关系。

接着看 Reflex 相关章节，重点不是公式细节，而是三个判断：为什么 verifier 的延迟误差在邻近位置仍可用；alignment gate 如何决定何时修正；candidate-boundary safeguard 为什么必要。这里最值得深挖的是，它其实在利用 rollout 轨迹内部的短程误差相关性，这和很多训练系统只做全局平均统计不同。

实验部分优先看主表和 ablation。主表看三件事：对 vanilla GRPO 的 generation/end-to-end 提升、对 FastGRPO 的 pairwise 优势、不同模型规模下收益是否稳定。消融则看 fast path、slow path、concurrency-aware budget 分别拿掉后的退化幅度。

如果时间有限，预计 25–35 分钟可以抓住主要贡献；如果要复现或迁移到自家 RL 系统，Reflex 触发条件、慢路径更新频率、tree budget 调度策略需要细读。

summary_en.core_problem: The paper targets a concrete bottleneck in RL post-training: GRPO-style training needs many long rollouts, and autoregressive generation dominates wall-clock time. Speculative decoding is a natural acceleration tool, but RL makes it harder because the target policy keeps changing. A static proposer quickly becomes stale, while continuously training a separate drafter adds backward passes, optimizer state, synchronization overhead, and extra KV-cache cost. The core problem is how to make speculative rollouts adapt to a non-stationary policy while preserving the exact target sampling distribution and keeping the system lightweight.
summary_en.importance: This is not a pretraining paper in the narrow sense, but it matters for the pretrain-to-post-train interface and for large-scale training systems. Its contribution is important in three ways. First, it extends exact speculative decoding from static inference into online RL rollouts, treating the rollout engine itself as part of the training algorithm. Second, it introduces a two-timescale adaptation scheme: local, gradient-free, within-trajectory correction for transient mismatch, and slower parameter updates for persistent drift. That separation is relevant beyond RL, including continual pretraining and other non-stationary training loops. Third, it avoids a standalone autoregressive drafter and instead uses lightweight future-token heads on top of the target hidden states, which is a cleaner and cheaper design.
summary_en.technical_approach:
SpecRoll is an exact speculative rollout engine built from four main pieces.

First, the proposer is not a separate drafter model. It uses MEDUSA-style future-token heads attached to the target backbone hidden state. Given a prefix, the target model samples an exact anchor token x_{t+1}, and multiple horizon heads predict later positions in parallel, reusing the target vocabulary projection. These candidates form a prefix-closed sparse tree. This removes the need for a second autoregressive backbone and its KV cache, reducing proposal cost and simplifying synchronization.

Second, verification remains exact and is made concurrency-aware. In GRPO, the number of active rollouts changes over time because some responses finish earlier than others. A fixed speculative tree is therefore inefficient: too expensive when concurrency is high, and too small to saturate hardware when concurrency drops. SpecRoll adjusts the sparse-tree budget based on active concurrency, using a smaller budget early and a larger one later. The objective is not just better acceptance on a single sequence, but better throughput for the whole rollout stage.

Third, the fast adaptation path is Reflex. The key observation is that delayed verifier errors can still be predictive for nearby future positions within the same trajectory. Reflex converts such mature verifier feedback into bounded, trajectory-local hidden-state corrections without backpropagation. It is guarded by a conservative alignment gate, which activates only when past errors are predictive of future mismatch, and by candidate-boundary safeguards that suppress harmful interventions near unstable boundaries. The design explicitly separates transient local mismatch from persistent drift.

Fourth, the slow path updates the future-token heads only when sustained degradation is detected. In other words, SpecRoll does not treat every mismatch as an online learning problem. It first uses Reflex to absorb short-lived, local errors, and only escalates recurring cross-trajectory mismatch into parameter updates. This differs from FastGRPO, where adaptation relies more heavily on continuously training a separate drafter.

Throughout the method, exact target verification is authoritative. The committed-token distribution is unchanged, so rewards, advantages, and the GRPO objective remain intact. The method changes rollout efficiency, not the RL objective.
summary_en.experiments:
The evaluation covers five models from 1.5B to 14B parameters and three math reasoning datasets, for 15 matched model-dataset settings. Against vanilla GRPO, SpecRoll reports 1.26x to 2.15x generation speedup and 1.21x to 2.04x end-to-end speedup. Against FastGRPO, it is better on both generation time and end-to-end time in all 15 matched settings, with an average pairwise end-to-end gain of 1.18x.

These results matter for two reasons. First, the gains are not limited to token-generation microbenchmarks; they carry through to the full RL training loop. Second, the combination of lightweight proposal heads and two-timescale adaptation appears more cost-effective than maintaining a separately trained online drafter, at least in the tested regime.

The ablations show that both the fast path and the slow path help individually, and the combination works best. That means Reflex is not a cosmetic add-on; it absorbs a meaningful portion of transient mismatch. At the same time, Reflex alone is insufficient because policy drift accumulates across trajectories, so slow parameter updates are still needed. Another useful finding is the role of the concurrency-aware tree budget, which explains why speculative decoding settings from ordinary inference do not transfer directly to RL rollouts.

The paper focuses on wall-clock and end-to-end efficiency rather than final reward improvements, which is consistent with the exact-verification design: the training signal should remain unchanged, while throughput improves.
summary_en.reading_guide:
This is a skim paper overall, but it is worth a closer read if you work on RL systems or post-training infrastructure.

Start with the introduction and isolate the main design choice relative to FastGRPO: instead of training a better standalone drafter, SpecRoll splits adaptation into local gradient-free correction and infrequent parameter updates. Then read Figure 2 and the method section around the proposal engine to understand the interaction among future-token heads, the anchor token, the sparse tree, and exact verification.

Next, focus on the Reflex section. The main questions are not the algebra but the mechanism: why delayed verifier errors remain useful locally, how the alignment gate decides when to intervene, and why candidate-boundary safeguards are necessary. The interesting systems idea is that the method exploits short-range error correlation inside a rollout trajectory.

In the experiments, prioritize the main timing table and the ablations. Check three things in the main results: gains over vanilla GRPO, pairwise wins over FastGRPO, and stability across model scales. In the ablations, look at what happens when the fast path, slow path, or concurrency-aware budget is removed.

If time is limited, 25 to 35 minutes is enough to capture the main idea. For implementation or reproduction, the most important details are the Reflex trigger conditions, the slow-path update schedule, and the tree-budget policy.

recommendation.en: Practical scheme for RL training rollout acceleration; focus on backprop-free hidden state correction in the Reflex module, directly reproducible for internal RLHF pipelines

paper.title: Optimizing What Policies Learn From: Recoverability-aware Rollout Intervention Learning
paper.abstract: Critic-free group-based reinforcement learning has become a scalable approach for post-training large language models. However, most existing methods allocate the same number of rollouts to every task and trajectory state, even though some rollouts provide much more useful learning signals than others. Recent work has started to treat rollout generation as an adaptive decision, but two important limitations remain. First, intervention strategies are often based on fixed heuristics and therefore

summary.core_problem: 这篇工作关注的是 group-based、critic-free RL 里另一个常被忽略的问题：rollout 预算通常被均匀分配，但不同任务、不同轨迹状态的学习价值差异很大。尤其在 agentic 或稀疏奖励场景里，有些状态再多采样也学不到东西，有些状态则值得额外分支探索。已有方法多用 reward variance、entropy、uncertainty 之类静态启发式来决定是否多采样，但这些信号会随着 policy 演化而失真，而且通常只能决定“多采几个”，不能表达“在什么位置、用什么方式介入”。论文要解决的核心问题，是如何在线学习一个结构化的 rollout intervention policy，让训练过程把算力花在更能产生学习信号的地方。
summary.importance: 对预训练研究的直接关系不如训练 recipe 论文强，但它对 post-training 里的数据效率、训练信号质量、以及“训练过程本身也可学习”这个方向有启发。它的重要性主要在两点。第一，它把 rollout allocation 从静态启发式提升为 outcome-driven 的在线学习问题，强调不是根据不确定性代理信号分配算力，而是根据干预后实际带来的学习信号增益来分配。第二，它把 intervention 从标量预算扩展到结构化决策空间，允许同时决定在哪里 branch、如何 branch。这种思路和 pretraining 中的 data curriculum、active data selection、adaptive compute allocation 有相通之处：关键不是平均地看 token 或样本，而是识别哪些位置更值得额外计算。
summary.technical_approach:
方法叫 Recoverability-Aware Intervention Learning，简称 RAIL。核心概念是 recoverability。按作者的定义，recoverability 衡量的是：在某个任务或轨迹状态上施加 intervention 后，reward-distribution signal 能提升多少。这里的重点不是最终 reward 本身，而是干预是否让训练看到更有区分度、更有学习价值的回报分布。

围绕这个概念，RAIL 做了三层设计。

第一，它把 rollout intervention 建模成一个 online contextual bandit。context 是当前任务或轨迹状态，action 是一个结构化 intervention 选择，observed utility 是实际观测到的 recoverability gain。这样做的意义是，controller 学到的是“在当前 policy、当前状态分布下，什么干预最能带来额外学习信号”，而不是依赖固定规则。作者明确把这一步用来弥补 non-stationary gap：policy 在变，干预策略也应跟着学。

第二，action space 不是单一的 rollout 数量，而是 structured intervention space。虽然给出的全文片段没有展开全部细节，但从引言和方法定义看，至少包括在哪里 branch、采用哪种 intervention strategy 等耦合决策。作者把这一步用来弥补 non-scalar gap：很多有价值的干预不是“多采样几个”这么简单，而是要在正确的状态、以正确的方式扩展轨迹。

第三，部署方式采用 shadow-to-live procedure。先用一个短 shadow phase 收集 intervention traces 和 supervision，不直接让 learned controller 影响主训练；等 controller 对 utility 有一定把握后，再进入 utility-gated live phase，选择性地把它接入 policy optimization。这个设计比较务实，因为在线学 intervention policy 容易把训练搞偏，先 shadow 再 live 相当于给 controller 一个冷启动缓冲区，也降低了早期错误干预的代价。

从整体上看，RAIL 不是改 GRPO 的 policy gradient 公式，而是改 rollout generation process。它把 rollout 生成从固定程序变成可学习、可适应的训练环节。和基于 entropy、variance 的启发式 branching 方法相比，差别在于：RAIL 关心的是 intervention 的 realized utility，而不是某个代理指标是否高。
summary.experiments:
论文声称从四个维度评估：effectiveness、adaptivity、expressiveness、efficiency，并在多个 benchmark 上优于现有 heuristic intervention baselines。给出的全文片段没有包含完整实验表和具体数字，因此无法可靠复述提升幅度、模型规模或数据规模。

从作者描述可以确认的实验结论有几条。第一，learned recoverability controller 比静态启发式更能适应 policy 演化，说明 non-stationary gap 不是表面问题，而会真实影响 rollout allocation 的收益。第二，结构化 intervention 比单纯调 rollout 数量更有效，说明 non-scalar gap 也成立。第三，shadow-to-live 机制不是纯工程包装，而是保证在线部署稳定性的关键部分。

如果后续阅读全文，实验部分最值得核对的是三类证据：一是 recoverability gain 与最终训练收益之间的相关性是否稳定；二是 learned controller 在训练早中晚期的决策分布如何变化；三是相对启发式方法，RAIL 的额外控制器开销是否被 rollout 节省抵消。如果这些证据完整，这篇工作的说服力会明显 stronger。
summary.reading_guide:
这篇更适合泛读，重点看问题定义和训练框架，不必在第一次阅读时深究所有 bandit 细节。

建议先看 Introduction 和 Section 2.1，确认作者如何定义 recoverability，以及它和 reward variance、entropy 这类常见代理信号有什么区别。这里是整篇文章最关键的判断基础：如果 recoverability 只是换个名字包装旧信号，价值就有限；如果它真的是 outcome-based utility，就有方法论意义。

然后看方法部分关于 contextual bandit 和 structured intervention space 的定义，重点理解 action space 到底包含哪些决策维度，以及 controller 的输入特征来自哪里。再看 shadow-to-live deployment，这部分决定方法是否能在真实训练环路里稳定工作。

实验部分优先看四类评估：effectiveness 看最终收益，adaptivity 看随 policy 演化是否持续有效，expressiveness 看结构化 action 是否优于标量预算，efficiency 看控制器开销和 rollout 节省的平衡。

如果只是判断是否值得跟进，20–30 分钟足够；如果要迁移到自家 RL pipeline，需要补看附录里的 intervention space、utility 定义、以及 online update 细节。

summary_en.core_problem: The paper studies a neglected inefficiency in critic-free, group-based RL: rollout budgets are usually allocated uniformly even though the learning value of additional rollouts varies sharply across tasks and trajectory states. This is especially problematic in agentic or sparse-reward settings, where some states are effectively unrecoverable while others would benefit from extra branching. Existing methods mostly rely on static heuristics such as reward variance, entropy, or uncertainty, but those proxies drift as the policy changes and usually only answer a scalar question like how many more rollouts to sample. The core problem is how to learn an online, structured rollout-intervention policy that spends compute where it produces more useful learning signal.
summary_en.importance: Its connection to pretraining is indirect, but it is relevant to post-training data efficiency, signal quality, and the broader idea that the training process itself can be optimized. The main contribution is conceptual. First, it reframes rollout allocation as an outcome-driven online learning problem rather than a heuristic scheduling problem. Compute is allocated based on realized intervention utility, not on static proxy signals. Second, it expands intervention from a scalar budget decision to a structured action space, allowing the system to decide both where and how to intervene. That is closely related in spirit to adaptive compute allocation, curriculum design, and active data selection in pretraining.
summary_en.technical_approach:
RAIL stands for Recoverability-Aware Intervention Learning. Its central concept is recoverability, defined as how much an intervention improves the reward-distribution signal at a task or trajectory state. The emphasis is not just on final reward, but on whether the intervention exposes more informative reward contrast for learning.

The method has three main layers.

First, rollout intervention is formulated as an online contextual bandit. The context is the current task or trajectory state, the action is a structured intervention choice, and the observed utility is the realized recoverability gain. This directly addresses the non-stationary gap: as the policy evolves, the intervention policy should also adapt from observed outcomes rather than remain a fixed heuristic.

Second, the action space is structured rather than scalar. From the paper’s framing, it includes coupled decisions such as where to branch and which intervention strategy to apply, not merely how many additional rollouts to generate. This addresses the non-scalar gap: useful intervention often depends on acting at the right state with the right branching pattern, not just increasing sample count.

Third, deployment uses a shadow-to-live procedure. A short shadow phase collects intervention traces and supervision without directly affecting the main optimization loop. Once the controller has enough signal, a utility-gated live phase selectively applies it during policy optimization. This is a practical design choice because online intervention learning can destabilize training if deployed too early; the shadow phase acts as a cold-start buffer.

Overall, RAIL does not modify the GRPO gradient formula itself. It modifies the rollout-generation process, turning it from a fixed procedure into an adaptive, learned component of training. Relative to entropy- or variance-based branching heuristics, the key difference is that RAIL optimizes for realized intervention utility rather than a proxy statistic.
summary_en.experiments:
The paper states that it evaluates RAIL along four axes: effectiveness, adaptivity, expressiveness, and efficiency, and that it outperforms heuristic intervention baselines across multiple benchmarks. However, the provided full-text excerpt does not include the detailed result tables, model sizes, dataset sizes, or exact gains, so those numbers cannot be reproduced reliably here.

What can be inferred from the text is still useful. First, the learned recoverability controller appears to adapt better than static heuristics as the policy changes, which supports the claim that the non-stationary gap is real. Second, structured intervention outperforms scalar budget control, supporting the non-scalar argument. Third, the shadow-to-live mechanism is presented as an important stability device rather than a cosmetic engineering detail.

When reading the full paper, the most important experimental checks are: whether recoverability gain correlates consistently with downstream training improvement; how the controller’s decisions evolve over the course of training; and whether the controller overhead is offset by rollout savings relative to heuristic baselines. Those points determine how convincing the method really is.
summary_en.reading_guide:
This is best treated as a skim paper. Focus on the problem formulation and the training-loop design rather than every bandit detail on the first pass.

Start with the introduction and the section that defines recoverability. The key question is whether recoverability is genuinely an outcome-based utility measure or just a relabeling of familiar proxies like entropy or reward variance. That distinction determines the paper’s value.

Then read the method section around the contextual-bandit formulation and the structured intervention space. Pay attention to what decisions are actually included in the action space and what features the controller observes. After that, read the shadow-to-live deployment procedure carefully, because that is what makes the method plausible in a real online training loop.

In the experiments, prioritize the four evaluation axes. Effectiveness tells you whether the method improves training. Adaptivity tells you whether it remains useful as the policy changes. Expressiveness tells you whether structured actions matter beyond scalar budgets. Efficiency tells you whether the controller overhead is justified.

If the goal is triage, 20 to 30 minutes is enough. For implementation, you would need the appendix details on the intervention space, the utility definition, and the online update rule.

recommendation.zh: 后训练RL中自适应分配rollout信号的思路可迁移到预训练的数据课程与训练信号筛选，重点看上下文bandit建模部分。
recommendation.en: Adaptive rollout allocation in post-training RL transfers to pretraining data curriculum and signal filtering; focus on the contextual bandit formulation.

paper.title: EASy: Towards Efficient LLM-Based Agentic System
paper.abstract: Agentic systems have emerged as a promising paradigm for solving complex tasks by coordinating specialized LLM-based agents. However, most existing systems primarily optimize task success while giving limited consideration to execution efficiency under practical constraints such as executor capability and computational cost. Existing router-based methods have limited ability to reason over rich, evolving task contexts, multi-step dependencies, and intermediate execution feedback, and often gener

summary.core_problem: 这篇工作解决的是异构 LLM agent 系统里的一个老问题：如何让 orchestrator 不只追求任务成功率，还能在真实约束下同时考虑执行器能力、调用成本、延迟和中间反馈，学会做动态、分阶段、可泛化的调度决策。现有 router 往往是轻量分类器或打分器，适合单步分发，不擅长处理长程依赖、任务分解、并行执行和执行后再规划；固定工作流则更难适应任务过程中不断变化的上下文。EASy 把这个问题表述成一个可训练的 sequential decision problem：给定一组能力和成本不同的 executors，由 LLM orchestrator 在 milestone 级别做分解、规划、分配和重规划，并用强化学习直接优化性能与效率的折中。
summary.importance: 对基座预训练本身，它不是直接的 pretrain recipe 论文；但对 pretrain↔posttrain 接口有现实意义。第一，它把“模型能力”与“系统级成本”放进同一个训练目标里，这和近来 RLVR、test-time compute allocation、mixture routing 的研究方向是连着的。第二，它说明如果要让 LLM 学会资源感知决策，仅靠静态 prompt 或外部 router 不够，训练信号需要覆盖中间状态、分支策略和不完整轨迹。第三，它提供了一种把 executor profile 显式写入上下文、再通过 RL 学习泛化到未见执行器的做法，这对未来的 model routing、tool routing、MoE-style external expert selection 都有参考价值。贡献量级更像系统训练范式上的扎实推进，而不是改变基座建模范式。
summary.technical_approach: 方法核心有三层。第一层是 milestone-plan-act 工作流。orchestrator 先把复杂任务拆成若干 milestones，而不是直接细到原子步骤。这样做有两个目的：一是减少低层执行噪声，让策略学习看到更稳定的状态转移；二是给并行执行留空间，因为 milestone 内部可以构建 dependency-aware execution graph，把互不依赖的步骤并发交给不同 executors。第二层是显式 executor profiling。每个 executor 都带有能力描述和成本信息，orchestrator 在决策时不仅看任务内容，也看“谁更强、谁更贵、谁适合当前子任务”。这和传统 router 只基于 query embedding 或历史统计做分发不同，EASy 让调度模型直接在语言上下文里推理 executor 的 profile，因此更容易适应 executor 集合变化。第三层是 end-to-end RL 训练。作者采用 tree-structured rollout，从一个初始轨迹出发，对 milestone 节点或 plan 节点展开替代分支，得到在相近上下文下的多种策略样本。奖励由三部分组成：任务正确性、执行效率、轨迹完整性。前两项对应效果与成本，后一项用于避免策略通过提前终止或局部完成来投机。奖励还做了 node-level 和 query-level normalization，目的是让不同分支、不同任务之间的学习信号可比，降低高方差。和普通单轨迹 RL 相比，这种树状展开更像在局部决策点上做 counterfactual exploration，监督密度更高，也更适合多步 orchestration。
summary.experiments: 全文给出的实验覆盖三类任务：数学推理、具身决策、deep research。摘要明确声称 EASy 在 performance-efficiency trade-off 上稳定优于现有 agentic baselines，且消融显示 milestone-plan-act、tree rollout、reward design 和对未见 executors 的泛化能力都各自有明显贡献。就论文定位看，关键结果不是单纯最高成功率，而是在相同或更低成本下取得更高任务完成度，或者在相同成功率下显著降低 executor 开销。作者还特别强调了 generalization to unseen executors，这一点比很多只在固定 executor pool 上调 prompt 的系统更有方法价值。当前给出的全文片段没有包含完整表格数字、模型规模、训练步数和具体成本降幅，因此无法安全填写精确数值；但从实验设计可以确认，论文重点看的是 Pareto front，而不是单点 accuracy。读的时候应特别留意：1）效率指标如何定义，是否统一折算为 token cost / latency / API cost；2）tree rollout 的分支深度和扩展策略；3）reward normalization 是否显著改善训练稳定性；4）未见 executor 泛化实验到底是 profile 改写、能力替换，还是新增 executor。
summary.reading_guide: 泛读建议先抓三处。第一看方法总览图和 milestone-plan-act 的例子，理解它为什么不做 step-level 全细粒度规划。第二看 RL 训练部分，重点是 tree-structured rollout 如何选节点扩展、奖励三项各自怎么定义、normalization 怎么做。第三看主结果图，确认作者比较的是成功率、成本和两者折中，而不是只报一个 aggregate score。预计 25–35 分钟能抓住主线。如果只想判断是否值得深读，优先看 introduction、method overview、reward design、generalization/ablation 四部分。需要带着一点保留：这类 agent orchestration 论文常见问题是 benchmark 依赖较强、成本模型容易任务特定、以及 RL 收益是否来自更强的 search budget 而非更好的 policy。读实验时要主动检查这些点。

summary_en.core_problem: The paper tackles a practical orchestration problem in heterogeneous LLM agent systems: how to train an orchestrator that does not optimize only task success, but also reasons over executor capability, cost, latency, intermediate feedback, and changing task context. Existing routers are usually lightweight predictors for one-shot dispatch. They are weak at multi-step dependencies, adaptive replanning, and generalization to unseen executors. EASy formulates orchestration as a trainable sequential decision problem where an LLM orchestrator decomposes a task into milestones, plans dependency-aware execution, assigns executors, and updates decisions based on intermediate outcomes, while reinforcement learning directly optimizes the performance-efficiency trade-off.
summary_en.importance: This is not a pretraining paper in the narrow sense, but it matters for the pretrain-to-posttrain interface. First, it puts model capability and system cost into one training objective, which is closely related to current work on RLVR, compute allocation, and routing under resource constraints. Second, it shows that resource-aware decision making is hard to get from prompting or static routers alone; the training signal needs to cover intermediate states, alternative branches, and incomplete trajectories. Third, the explicit use of executor profiles inside the context, combined with RL for generalization to unseen executors, is relevant to future model routing, tool routing, and even external-expert selection in MoE-like systems. The contribution is best read as a solid systems-and-training advance rather than a new base modeling paradigm.
summary_en.technical_approach: The method has three main components. First is the milestone-plan-act workflow. Instead of planning at the finest step granularity from the start, the orchestrator first decomposes a complex query into milestones. This reduces low-level execution noise and gives the policy a more stable state abstraction. Within each milestone, it builds a dependency-aware execution graph and can run independent steps in parallel across executors. Second is explicit executor profiling. Each executor comes with textual descriptions of capability and cost, so the orchestrator reasons jointly over task requirements and executor profiles rather than routing by query features alone. This differs from standard learned routers that often rely on shallow signals and fixed executor sets. Third is end-to-end RL with tree-structured rollout. Starting from an initial trajectory, the system expands selected milestone or plan nodes into alternative branches, producing multiple strategies under comparable contexts. Rewards combine task correctness, execution efficiency, and trajectory completeness. The completeness term is important because otherwise the policy may exploit partial execution or early stopping. Rewards are normalized at both node and query levels to make signals more comparable across branches and tasks and to reduce variance. Compared with standard single-trajectory RL, this branch-based exploration gives denser supervision around local decision points and is better aligned with multi-step orchestration.
summary_en.experiments: The experiments cover three task families: mathematical reasoning, embodied decision making, and deep research. The main claim is consistent improvement on the performance-efficiency frontier over prior agentic baselines. The key result is not simply higher success rate, but better task completion at the same or lower cost, or lower executor cost at comparable performance. The paper also emphasizes generalization to unseen executors, which is more informative than evaluations on a fixed executor pool. The provided full-content excerpt does not include the final tables with exact numbers, model sizes, training steps, or cost reductions, so it would be unsafe to invent precise metrics. Still, the experimental structure makes clear what to inspect: how efficiency is measured, whether cost is token-based or latency-based, how deep the rollout tree goes, whether reward normalization stabilizes training, and what “unseen executor” means operationally—new profiles, swapped capabilities, or newly introduced executors.
summary_en.reading_guide: For a quick pass, focus on three parts. First, read the method overview and the milestone-plan-act example to understand why the paper avoids fully atomic planning. Second, read the RL section carefully, especially node expansion in tree rollout, the three reward components, and the normalization scheme. Third, inspect the main result figures to verify that the comparison is really about the Pareto trade-off between performance and cost, not a single blended score. A 25–35 minute skim should be enough to capture the main ideas. If deciding whether it deserves deeper reading, prioritize the introduction, method overview, reward design, and the generalization/ablation sections. Keep a healthy skepticism on three common failure modes in this line of work: benchmark-specific cost models, gains that come from larger search budget rather than a better policy, and weak transfer outside the curated executor pool.

recommendation.zh: 只看 RL reward 和 unseen-executor 实验；若成本记账干净，它可作为 agentic test-time compute 分配的弱基线。
recommendation.en: Read the RL reward and unseen-executor experiments; if the cost accounting is clean, it is a useful weak baseline for agentic test-time compute allocation.

paper.title: ABSeeker: Training Long-Horizon Search Agents via Answer-Backtracked Credit Assignment
paper.abstract: Long-horizon search agents must make multiple sequential actions (steps) to search, retrieve, verify, and integrate evidence to reach a final answer. However, existing methods for training these agents typically treat all steps within a trajectory uniformly during both supervised fine-tuning (SFT) and reinforcement learning (RL), failing to distinguish useful actions from erroneous or redundant ones. In this paper, we propose Answer-Backtracked Credit Assignment (ABC), a fine-grained credit assi

summary.core_problem: 长程搜索agent训练存在信用分配难题：现有监督微调（SFT）和强化学习（RL）方法对轨迹内所有步骤统一加权，无法区分有用、错误或冗余动作，稀疏的二元轨迹级奖励无法为中间步骤提供有效监督信号。
summary.importance: 基于答案回溯构造稠密步级奖励的思路，可迁移到RL预训练、长程推理后训练等场景，为稀疏奖励下的细粒度监督信号设计提供参考。
summary.technical_approach: 提出Answer-Backtracked Credit Assignment（ABC）细粒度信用分配框架，分为两个阶段：1）答案回溯线索恢复：从已验证的标准答案出发，反推出解题所需的中间证据线索（实体、事实、关系）；2）线索锚定步级打分：用恢复的线索对搜索轨迹的每一步进行评估，判断该步是发现、验证、优化线索，还是错误推理，将稀疏的轨迹级二元奖励转化为稠密的步级奖励。基于该框架开发两种训练方法：ABC-SFT按步级奖励重加权每轮的SFT损失，ABC-GRPO将步级分数直接作为组相对策略优化（GRPO）的奖励信号。
summary.experiments: 基于Qwen3.5-4B训练ABSeeker模型，在BrowseComp上准确率37.3%，BrowseComp-ZH上39.1%，xbench-2505上77.0%，xbench-2510上46.0%，GAIA-text上81.6%。加入上下文管理机制后，BrowseComp和BrowseComp-ZH的性能分别提升至55.3%和52.9%，超过同规模4B基线（QUEST-4B、Dr. Venus）以及约30B参数的搜索agent（通义DeepResearch、OpenSeeker）。
summary.reading_guide: 泛读建议：重点看第3章的信用分配框架设计，以及第4章中步级奖励 vs 轨迹级奖励的消融实验，预计阅读时间15-20分钟。核心关注答案回溯构造稠密奖励的思路，无需深究搜索agent的工程实现细节。

summary_en.core_problem: Long-horizon search agent training faces a credit assignment challenge: existing supervised fine-tuning (SFT) and reinforcement learning (RL) methods treat all steps in a trajectory uniformly, failing to distinguish useful, erroneous, or redundant actions. Sparse binary trajectory-level rewards provide no effective supervision for intermediate steps.
summary_en.importance: The idea of constructing dense step-level rewards via answer backtracking is transferable to RL pretraining and long-horizon reasoning post-training, offering a reference for fine-grained supervision signal design under sparse reward settings.
summary_en.technical_approach: The proposed Answer-Backtracked Credit Assignment (ABC) framework has two core stages: 1) Answer-Backtracked Clue Recovery: starting from the verified ground-truth answer, it recovers intermediate evidence clues (entities, facts, relations) required to solve the query; 2) Clue-Anchored Step Scoring: it evaluates every step in the search trajectory against the recovered clues, classifying steps as clue discovery, verification, refinement, or incorrect reasoning, and converts sparse binary trajectory-level rewards into dense step-level scores. Two training variants are built on top: ABC-SFT reweights per-turn SFT loss by step reward, and ABC-GRPO uses step-level scores directly as rewards for Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO).
summary_en.experiments: Trained on Qwen3.5-4B, the ABSeeker model achieves 37.3% accuracy on BrowseComp, 39.1% on BrowseComp-ZH, 77.0% on xbench-2505, 46.0% on xbench-2510, and 81.6% on GAIA-text. With context management, performance on BrowseComp and BrowseComp-ZH improves to 55.3% and 52.9% respectively, outperforming same-scale 4B baselines (QUEST-4B, Dr. Venus) and ~30B parameter search agents (Tongyi DeepResearch, OpenSeeker).
summary_en.reading_guide: Skim recommendation: focus on Section 3 for the credit assignment framework design, and Section 4 for ablations comparing step-level vs trajectory-level rewards. Estimated reading time: 15-20 minutes. Prioritize the answer-backtracking idea for dense reward construction; skip detailed engineering of the search agent stack.

recommendation.zh: 答案回溯的信用分配思路对解决长程agent RL稀疏奖励问题有借鉴，重点看§3的ABC算法细节。
recommendation.en: The answer-backtracking credit assignment idea is informative for solving sparse reward problems in long-horizon agent RL; focus on §3 for ABC algorithm details.

paper.title: PI-Mem: Pushing Long-Context Reasoning to 3.6M Tokens with Parallel-Iterative Memory
paper.abstract: Long-context reasoning remains a critical bottleneck for large language models, as recent recurrent-memory approaches face two inherent challenges: sequential chunk-wise updates can overwrite early critical evidence with later irrelevant content, and serial inter-chunk dependencies limit parallelism and cause latency to increase with context length. To address these issues, we propose PI-Mem (Parallel-Iterative Memory), a mechanism that processes all chunks in parallel and iteratively refines a

summary.core_problem: 这篇工作处理的是超长上下文推理里的一个老问题：基于 recurrent memory 的方法虽然把计算从全局注意力里解放出来，但它们通常按 chunk 串行更新 memory，早期证据容易被后续无关内容覆盖，而且延迟会随 chunk 数线性增长。PI-Mem 试图同时解决这两个问题：既减少 memory overwrite，又把跨 chunk 处理改成并行。
summary.importance: 对基座预训练本身的直接影响有限，它更偏长上下文推理机制和 inference-time workflow；但对“如何在不重新训练超长上下文 backbone 的前提下扩展有效上下文”有现实意义。启发点主要有两处。第一，它把 memory 设计从单链式更新改成 bounded-turn 的并行-迭代 refinement，这是一种比传统 chunk-by-chunk memory 更稳的外部工作流。第二，它用 RL 直接优化整个 read-select-merge-answer 过程，并加入 turn-efficiency reward，说明这类长上下文控制流可以被当作一个可训练策略，而不只是 prompt engineering。若从预训练接口看，这类方法也提示了一个方向：未来长上下文能力不一定全靠 backbone 原生窗口扩展，也可以靠 memory policy 学出来。
summary.technical_approach:
PI-Mem 的核心是 Parallel-Iterative Memory。输入长文档后，先切成多个等长 chunks，并初始化一个空的全局 textual memory。每一轮 turn 包含 read、select、merge 三步。read 阶段中，所有 chunks 在同一个当前 memory 条件下并行处理，而不是像传统 recurrent memory 那样依赖前一个 chunk 更新后的 memory 再处理下一个 chunk。这样做有两个直接效果：一是避免后处理 chunk 对前面 memory 的逐步覆盖；二是 chunk 之间没有串行依赖，延迟更低。

select 阶段从每个 chunk 的读出结果里筛选“新的或互补的证据”，目的是减少冗余写入。merge 阶段把这些候选证据压缩进新的共享 memory，供下一轮所有 chunks 再次并行读取。关键点在于，下一轮读取时，每个 chunk 都能看到上一轮从其他 chunk 汇总出的全局证据，因此跨 chunk 的信息整合不是靠单次串行传播，而是靠多轮共享 memory 的迭代 refinement。作者还设计了 adaptive exit：当没有 chunk 再提供有用新证据，或达到最大 turn 数 K 时停止，再基于问题和最终 memory 生成答案。

训练上，作者不是监督每一步 memory 内容，而是把整个流程端到端用 RL 优化。奖励由两部分组成：answer accuracy reward 和 turn-efficiency reward。前者鼓励最终答对，后者惩罚无效或冗余 turn，避免模型总是跑满最大轮数。这个设计的含义是，memory 更新策略、停止时机、证据筛选都被统一到一个策略学习问题里。和已有 recurrent-memory baseline 相比，PI-Mem 的区别不在于 memory 更大，而在于更新拓扑从“单链覆盖”变成“并行读取 + 共享迭代”。
summary.experiments:
文中主要在 Qwen3.5-35B-A3B 和 Qwen2.5-7B 上验证，任务集中在长上下文 QA，尤其强调 HotpotQA 在 3.6M tokens 条件下的表现。最核心的结果是：在 3.6M tokens 的 HQA 上，PI-Mem 相比 MemAgent 分别提升 +6.25 和 +7.81 个绝对点，并带来 6.1× 和 2.1× 的推理加速。这个结果对应两类收益：一类是准确率提升，说明并行-迭代 memory 确实比串行覆盖式 memory 更能保留和整合远距离证据；另一类是 latency 改善，说明并行 chunk 处理在超长输入下有实际系统价值。

从论文给出的训练设定看，作者强调 bounded number of turns，而不是无限迭代，因此成本主要由 chunk 并行度和 turn 数共同决定。turn-efficiency reward 的作用是让模型学会在证据已足够时尽早停止，而不是机械地多轮扫描。虽然给出的摘要片段里没有完整消融表，但从方法描述可以预期，关键消融应包括：去掉并行改回串行、去掉 iterative refinement 只做单轮、去掉 turn-efficiency reward、改变最大 turn 数 K、以及不同 chunk 粒度下的性能/延迟权衡。阅读时应重点确认这些消融是否支持作者关于 overwrite reduction 和 latency reduction 的两条主张。
summary.reading_guide:
泛读建议先看 Method 和主结果表。重点不是记住 read-select-merge 的字面流程，而是弄清楚它和传统 recurrent-memory agent 的依赖结构差异：传统方法是 chunk1→memory1→chunk2→memory2 的单链；PI-Mem 是所有 chunks 在同一 memory 下并行读，再统一更新 memory，然后进入下一轮。这个差异决定了它为什么更快，也决定了它为什么更不容易把早期证据冲掉。

如果只花 20 分钟，建议顺序是：Introduction 中的问题定义 → Figure 2 / Algorithm 1 → HotpotQA 3.6M 主结果 → RL reward 设计。若准备判断它是否适合自己的系统，还需要看附录里的 latency 测量方式、chunk 数与 turn 数设置、memory 长度限制，以及和 MemAgent 的公平对比条件。因为这类工作很容易在实现细节上影响结论，比如并行度假设、批处理方式、是否把多轮调用开销算进总时延。

summary_en.core_problem: The paper targets a persistent weakness of recurrent-memory approaches for ultra-long-context reasoning. Standard chunk-by-chunk memory updates are sequential: later chunks can overwrite early evidence before its relevance becomes clear, and inference latency grows with the number of chunks because each update depends on the previous one. PI-Mem is designed to address both issues at once by reducing overwrite and removing serial inter-chunk dependence.
summary_en.importance: Its direct relevance to core pretraining is limited; this is more about long-context reasoning workflow than backbone training. Still, it is useful for researchers thinking about how to extend effective context without retraining a native multi-million-token model. Two ideas stand out. First, it replaces single-chain recurrent memory with bounded-turn parallel iterative refinement, which is a cleaner control structure for evidence aggregation. Second, it trains the whole read-select-merge-answer process with RL, including a turn-efficiency reward, treating long-context control flow as a learnable policy rather than a fixed prompting recipe. From a pretrain-to-inference interface perspective, it suggests that some long-context capability can come from learned memory policy, not only from enlarging the backbone context window.
summary_en.technical_approach:
PI-Mem introduces Parallel-Iterative Memory. A long context is split into equal-sized chunks, and a global textual memory is initialized as empty. Each turn consists of three operations: read, select, and merge. In the read step, all chunks are processed in parallel conditioned on the same current global memory. This differs from standard recurrent-memory systems, where chunk i must wait for the memory updated by chunk i-1. The immediate consequences are lower latency and less risk that later chunks repeatedly overwrite a single evolving memory state before earlier evidence can be integrated.

In the select step, the model extracts observations from each chunk that contain new or complementary evidence. In the merge step, these observations are consolidated into an updated shared memory for the next turn. The important mechanism is that, in the next iteration, every chunk is read again under a memory that already contains evidence gathered from other chunks. Cross-chunk interaction therefore happens through iterative shared-memory refinement rather than through a single serial pass.
